title: Downtown parking strategy and 2025 capital budget
subtitle: Year-round parking enforcement, shuttle service, Bissell Park lot, Belwood Hall, new parks, roads, bridges and water projects
overview: The Committee of the Whole recommended that Council approve the Downtown Parking Strategy final report and a partial 2025 implementation plan, subject to budget approval. Staff proposed a move to year-round enforcement, a switch to an administrative monetary penalty system, and another year's pause on paid parking, with the downtown shuttle expanded if funding partners are found. {{vote:m1}}

The committee also recommended that staff include the 2025 preliminary draft capital budget in the 2025 draft budget. {{vote:m2}} The Operations Centre and Bissell Park multi-use surface projects were left out for now, and vehicle and equipment replacement amounts are still being updated. Projects discussed included Belwood Hall accessibility work, two new neighbourhood parks, Colborne Street, Hill Street East, the second phase of St David Street, the Fourth Line bridge, and the water meter replacement.

For residents, the decisions shape downtown parking rules and fees and the roads, parks and water infrastructure planned for 2025. Council still has to adopt these recommendations. The budget survey is expected in early October, with further budget discussion in November and December.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the draft Municipal Downtown Parking Strategy Final Report.

The committee recommended approval of the 2025 plan, subject to 2025 budget approval, covering year-round enforcement, a move to an administrative monetary penalty system, a further pause on paid parking, and shuttle and parking supply work.
The committee recommended delegating authority to the Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer to sign contracts and agreements for the 2025 Parking Implementation Plan.
The committee recommended that staff include the 2025 Preliminary Draft Capital Budget from report COR2024-51 in the 2025 Draft Budget.

debate: On parking, councillors supported pausing paid parking, year-round enforcement and the move to an administrative penalty system. One councillor said paid parking was not wanted by Fergus businesses and worried a pilot there was still listed in the report. Staff said no location had been chosen and the downtown business associations would be consulted.

Several councillors questioned paving the Bissell Park East lot because of its flood plain location and the amount of pavement. Staff said 2025 would only test use of the lot with signage and shuttle stops, and that the paving could be removed from the 10-year capital plan later. Councillors asked about alternatives such as grass pavers and noted the steep hill to the lot.

Councillors asked for more information on the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion budget item. Some said Council had not received enough detail on advisory committee work. Staff said policies needing approval will come to Council, and that minutes are not meant to record every discussion. Councillors and the mayor agreed members should report back more on their committees.

Downtown Fergus street lighting drew concern that replacing 20 fixtures may not be enough. A councillor raised safety, vandalism and dark areas. Staff said other projects cover wiring and added lighting on St Patrick Street. Decorative lighting is usually added during full street reconstruction because of the cost of burying overhead wires.

On Belwood Hall, councillors asked whether the larger budget would serve seniors and the wider community, and how it fits with the parks and recreation master plan. Staff said options and costs will come back to Council before construction. Councillors also asked how water and wastewater projects are paid for. Staff said water and sewer rates, not property taxes, cover them.
